segments.t: Wearing his spotless white shirt, Manager Zhou stops beside Qing and Chen in the hallway and reaches eagerly for the small corner brush. Let's listen in first.
多好看的花园绿呀！给我一把刷子——老板也得帮忙！
老板，您穿着雪白的衬衫，还穿着擦亮的皮鞋呢。
就刷底下整整齐齐的三根木条！我的手很稳，你们看！
周经理，当心，您的袖子离湿油漆只有两厘米——
完全没碰到衬衫！哈！等等……我的鼻子有点痒。
周经理，别抬拿绿刷子的那只手——！
你们俩为什么那样盯着我的额头看？
因为您刚把老花镜左边的镜片刷成了亮绿色。
我的眼镜又架在额头上了？！哎呀，眼前全像一片森林！
站好别动！温水加软布——一擦就掉了！
跟新的一样干净！谢谢你，小晴……我想我还是去前台盯着吧。
明智的决定，老板。湿油漆交给我们吧。
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
多好看的花园绿呀！给我一把刷子——老板也得帮忙！
'What a lovely garden green! Give me a brush—the owner must help too!' Starting with the word for 'how much' turns 'good-looking' into 'what a lovely colour!', an easy way to admire anything aloud.
老板，您穿着雪白的衬衫，还穿着擦亮的皮鞋呢。
'Boss, you are wearing a snow-white shirt and polished black shoes.' Notice two vivid compounds side by side: 'snow-white' for the shirt and 'leather-shoes'—literally 'skin-shoes'—for dress shoes.
就刷底下整整齐齐的三根木条！我的手很稳，你们看！
'Just three neat slats on the bottom! I have a steady hand, watch!' Repeating each half of 'neat' makes a four-beat rhythm—'neat-neat-even-even'—showing off how tidy Zhou plans to be.
周经理，当心，您的袖子离湿油漆只有两厘米——
'Careful, Manager Zhou, your sleeve is two centimetres from the wet edge—' Qing says 'guard your heart' for 'careful!' and still keeps the polite 'you' even while warning her boss.
完全没碰到衬衫！哈！等等……我的鼻子有点痒。
'Missed my shirt completely! Ha! Wait... my nose itches.' Before an unpleasant feeling like 'itchy' or 'tired', Mandarin slips in 'have a bit' so it sounds natural rather than blunt.
周经理，别抬拿绿刷子的那只手——！
'Manager Zhou, don't lift the hand holding the green brush—!' Mandarin puts the whole description—'holding the green brush'—before 'that hand', saving the danger for the final word.
你们俩为什么那样盯着我的额头看？
'Why are you both staring at my forehead like that?' Adding one short syllable after 'you-plural' means 'you two', a friendly everyday shortcut for any pair of people.
因为您刚把老花镜左边的镜片刷成了亮绿色。
'Because you just painted the left lens of your reading glasses bright green.' Reading glasses have a charming name in Chinese: literally 'old-blurry mirrors', for eyes that blur with age.
我的眼镜又架在额头上了？！哎呀，眼前全像一片森林！
'My glasses were on my forehead again?! Oh, everything looks like a forest!' Zhou's running habit strikes again—and Mandarin says 'in front of the eyes' for 'everything I see'.
站好别动！温水加软布——一擦就掉了！
'Stand completely still! Warm water and a soft cloth—off it comes!' Pairing 'one' with 'right away'—literally 'one wipe, right away off'—captures something coming clean on the first try.
跟新的一样干净！谢谢你，小晴……我想我还是去前台盯着吧。
'Clean as new! Thank you, Qing... I think I will go supervise the front desk.' Here 'still is' means 'I had better just', the sheepish phrase you reach for when retreating to Plan B.
明智的决定，老板。湿油漆交给我们吧。
'Wise decision, boss. Leave the wet paint to us.' Literally 'hand over to us', that reassuring chunk works whenever you take a job off someone's hands.
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.
多好看的花园绿呀！给我一把刷子——老板也得帮忙！
老板，您穿着雪白的衬衫，还穿着擦亮的皮鞋呢。
就刷底下整整齐齐的三根木条！我的手很稳，你们看！
周经理，当心，您的袖子离湿油漆只有两厘米——

周经理，别抬拿绿刷子的那只手——！
你们俩为什么那样盯着我的额头看？
因为您刚把老花镜左边的镜片刷成了亮绿色。
我的眼镜又架在额头上了？！哎呀，眼前全像一片森林！
站好别动！温水加软布——一擦就掉了！
跟新的一样干净！谢谢你，小晴……我想我还是去前台盯着吧。
明智的决定，老板。湿油漆交给我们吧。
White shirt spared, green glasses rescued in time, and Manager Zhou retreats safely to dry ground at the front desk! See you next time.
再见！
